lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.t: Greeting and the call to unity
nodes.d: Paul thanks God for the grace given to the Corinthians, then appeals to them to end their divisions over which leader they follow.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why following one teacher against another is wrong, using 1 Corinthians 1:10-13?
ev: Quote the slogans the Corinthians were using (1:12)
Explain why Paul says Christ is not divided (1:13)

nodes.t: 1 Corinthians: overview
nodes.d: Paul writes to the church at Corinth about divisions, sin in the church, questions they asked him, worship, the resurrection and the collection (1:1-16:24).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short outline of 1 Corinthians and name three problems Paul corrects in the Corinthian church?
ev: Name the main problems Paul addresses: divisions, immorality, lawsuits, marriage, food offered to idols, the Lord's supper, gifts, the resurrection
Say who the letter is addressed to from 1:2

nodes.t: The cross: God's wisdom and power
nodes.d: Paul says the preaching of the cross looks foolish to those perishing but is the power of God to those being saved, and that God chose the weak and low so that no one may boast.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says the cross is God's wisdom and power, using 1 Corinthians 1:18-31?
ev: Contrast how the cross is seen by those perishing and by those saved (1:18)
List who God chose according to 1:26-29 and why (1:29)
Name what Christ is made to us (1:30)

nodes.t: The Spirit reveals God's hidden wisdom
nodes.d: Paul preached Christ crucified in weakness, and says the wisdom of God, hidden from this world's rulers, is revealed by the Spirit and understood only spiritually.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain, using 1 Corinthians 2, how a person comes to understand the things of God?
ev: State what Paul determined to know among the Corinthians (2:2)
Explain who knows the things of God and how we receive them (2:10-12)
Contrast the natural man and the spiritual person (2:14-15)

nodes.t: Servants, builders and God's temple
nodes.d: Paul tells the divided Corinthians that he and Apollos are only servants, that God gives the increase, that Jesus Christ is the one foundation, and that the church is God's temple.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who gives growth in the church and what the foundation is, using 1 Corinthians 3?
ev: Explain the picture of planting and watering (3:6-7)
Say what the one foundation is (3:11)
Explain what happens to each builder's work (3:12-15)
Say why the church is called God's temple (3:16-17)

nodes.t: Faithful stewards and the apostles as fathers
nodes.d: Paul says ministers are stewards who must be found faithful, whom the Lord will judge; he contrasts the Corinthians' pride with the apostles' sufferings and warns that he will come.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says it is a small thing to be judged by men, using 1 Corinthians 4:1-7?
ev: Say what is required of stewards (4:2)
Explain who is to judge and when (4:4-5)
Answer Paul's question in 4:7 about what we have that we did not receive

nodes.t: Dealing with sin in the church
nodes.d: Paul rebukes the church for tolerating a case of sexual immorality, tells them to put the person out, and explains that they must judge those inside the church while God judges those outside.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul tells the Corinthians to put away the wicked person, using 1 Corinthians 5?
ev: Describe the sin reported in 5:1 and the church's attitude (5:2)
Explain the picture of leaven (5:6-8)
Explain the difference between those within and those without (5:9-13)

nodes.t: Lawsuits among believers
nodes.d: Paul asks why Christians take each other to law before unbelievers, reminds them that the saints will judge the world, and warns that the unrighteous will not inherit the kingdom.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain 1 Corinthians 6:11 and why it matters for how believers treat each other?
ev: Say where Paul wants disputes settled and why (6:1-5)
List the kinds of people who will not inherit the kingdom (6:9-10)
Quote the three things Paul says happened to the Corinthians in 6:11

nodes.t: Your body is the Lord's temple
nodes.d: Paul teaches that the body is for the Lord, not for sexual immorality, that believers are members of Christ and the Spirit's temple, and that they were bought with a price.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says our bodies belong to God, using 1 Corinthians 6:19-20?
ev: Explain why the body is not for fornication (6:13-15)
Say what Paul tells them to do about fornication (6:18)
Explain what it means that believers are bought with a price (6:19-20)

nodes.t: Marriage, singleness and calling
nodes.d: Answering the Corinthians' letter, Paul teaches about the duties of husband and wife, the unmarried and widows, believers married to unbelievers, and living in the calling in which one was called.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarize what Paul says in 1 Corinthians 7:1-24 about marriage and about staying in the calling in which we were called?
ev: Describe the mutual duty of husband and wife (7:3-4)
Say what Paul teaches about a believer with an unbelieving spouse (7:12-16)
Explain the rule of 7:17, 7:20 and 7:24

nodes.t: The unmarried, widows and the shortness of time
nodes.d: Paul gives his judgment about virgins and the unmarried in view of the present distress, says the time is short, and explains that the unmarried can attend upon the Lord without distraction.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says in 1 Corinthians 7:35 that he writes these things, and what he does not mean to do?
ev: Say whether Paul calls marriage a sin (7:28)
Explain why he says the time is short (7:29-31)
State the condition for a widow's remarriage (7:39)

nodes.t: Knowledge, love and food offered to idols
nodes.d: Paul says an idol is nothing and there is one God and one Lord, but that knowledge puffs up while love builds up, so believers must not cause a weak brother to stumble.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul would give up eating meat rather than make a brother stumble, using 1 Corinthians 8:13?
ev: State the confession of 8:6
Explain the difference between knowledge and love in 8:1
Explain how a believer can wound a weak conscience (8:9-12)

nodes.t: Paul's rights given up for the gospel
nodes.d: Paul defends his apostleship and his right to be supported, but says he has not used that right, becoming all things to all people so that he might save some.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul gave up his rights, using 1 Corinthians 9:19-23?
ev: List the rights Paul says he has (9:4-6)
Explain why he did not use them (9:12, 9:18)
Explain what Paul means by becoming all things to all men (9:19-22)

nodes.t: Running the race with discipline
nodes.d: Paul compares the Christian life to a race and to a fight that requires self-control, so that he is not disqualified after preaching to others.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul means by running to obtain an incorruptible crown (1 Corinthians 9:24-27)?
ev: Describe the two pictures Paul uses (race and fight)
Explain what Paul does to his body and why (9:27)

nodes.t: Warnings from Israel in the wilderness
nodes.d: Paul reminds the Corinthians that Israel passed through the sea and ate and drank spiritual food, yet many fell; he says these things were examples to us, and that God provides a way of escape from temptation.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul uses Israel's failures as a warning, and what God promises in 1 Corinthians 10:13?
ev: List the privileges of Israel in 10:1-4 and the sins in 10:7-10
Explain why Paul says these things were written (10:11)
State the promise of 10:13

nodes.t: The Lord's table and the table of demons
nodes.d: Paul tells believers to flee idolatry, explaining that the cup and bread are communion in Christ's blood and body, and that they cannot share both the Lord's table and the table of demons.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says we cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of devils (1 Corinthians 10:21)?
ev: Explain what the cup and the bread are called in 10:16
Say why believers cannot partake of both tables (10:20-21)

nodes.t: Liberty, conscience and the glory of God
nodes.d: Paul gives practical rules for eating what is sold in the market or served at a feast, tells believers to seek the good of others, and sums up: do all to the glory of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} apply 1 Corinthians 10:31 to an everyday choice and explain how seeking another's good fits with it?
ev: State the rule of 10:31
Explain what to do when someone says the food was offered to idols (10:28-29)
Say whom Paul asks them to follow (11:1)

nodes.t: Order in worship: headship and head coverings
nodes.d: Paul praises the Corinthians for keeping the traditions, teaches about headship and about men and women praying or prophesying, and says the churches have no other custom.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says about headship in 1 Corinthians 11:3 and 11:11-12 without leaving out either passage?
ev: State the order of headship in 11:3
Say what practices Paul addresses for men and women in 11:4-7
Note that Paul says man and woman are not independent of each other in the Lord (11:11-12)

nodes.t: The Lord's supper
nodes.d: Paul rebukes the Corinthians for how they ate together, then recounts what he received from the Lord about the bread and the cup, calls the cup the new testament in Christ's blood, and tells them to examine themselves.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what Paul says about the bread and the cup in 1 Corinthians 11:23-26 and explain what it means to examine oneself?
ev: Describe the abuses in 11:20-22
Retell the institution of the supper from 11:23-25
Explain what the supper shows until the Lord comes (11:26)
Say what Paul tells each person to do before eating (11:28)

nodes.t: One Spirit, many gifts
nodes.d: Paul says that no one confesses Jesus as Lord except by the Holy Ghost and that the one Spirit gives different gifts to each person for the common good.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the gifts differ but come from the same Spirit, using 1 Corinthians 12:4-11?
ev: State the test of 12:3
List some gifts named in 12:8-10
Explain who decides how gifts are distributed (12:11)

nodes.t: One body, many members
nodes.d: Paul compares the church to a body with many members that need one another, naming various roles God has set in the church.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} use the picture of the body in 1 Corinthians 12 to explain why every church member matters?
ev: Explain how we all became one body (12:13)
Explain why no member can say it has no need of another (12:21)
Say what happens when one member suffers (12:26)

nodes.t: The more excellent way: love
nodes.d: Paul says that gifts, knowledge and sacrifice are nothing without love, describes what love is and does, and says that faith, hope and love remain, the greatest being love.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why love is greater than gifts, using 1 Corinthians 13?
ev: List things love does and does not do (13:4-7)
Say what will cease and what never fails (13:8)
Name the three that abide (13:13)

nodes.t: Tongues, prophecy and order in the assembly
nodes.d: Paul urges them to seek gifts that build up the church, especially prophecy, requires tongues to be interpreted, regulates speaking in turn, and ends by saying all things should be done decently and in order.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the purpose Paul gives for all speaking in church (14:26) and the rules in 1 Corinthians 14:27-33?
ev: Explain why Paul prefers prophecy in church (14:3-5)
State the rules for tongues and prophets (14:27-32)
Say why God is not the author of confusion (14:33)
Read 14:34-35 carefully and say what it commands about speaking in the churches

nodes.t: The gospel: Christ died and rose
nodes.d: Paul reminds the Corinthians of the gospel he received and preached, that Christ died for our sins, was buried and rose the third day according to the scriptures, and was seen by many witnesses.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} state the gospel in the words of 1 Corinthians 15:3-4 and name some who saw the risen Christ?
ev: Recite the gospel summary from 15:3-4
List the witnesses named in 15:5-8
Explain what Paul says about himself in 15:9-10

nodes.t: If Christ is not raised: the firstfruits
nodes.d: Paul argues that if there is no resurrection of the dead then Christ is not risen and faith is vain, but Christ is risen as the firstfruits, as Adam brought death and Christ brings life, until death is destroyed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the resurrection of Christ matters for the believer, using 1 Corinthians 15:12-22?
ev: List the consequences if Christ is not risen (15:14-19)
Explain Adam and Christ in 15:21-22
Say what the last enemy is (15:26)

nodes.t: The resurrection body and the victory over death
nodes.d: Paul answers how the dead are raised, with the picture of a seed, contrasts the natural and spiritual body and the first and last Adam, and describes believers being changed at the last trumpet with death swallowed up in victory.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Paul says will happen to the dead in Christ and to the living, using 1 Corinthians 15:42-58?
ev: Explain the seed picture (15:36-38)
Contrast sown and raised in 15:42-44
Explain how believers will be changed (15:51-53)
State the closing exhortation of 15:58

nodes.t: The collection, plans and closing greetings
nodes.d: Paul gives orders for the collection for the saints, his travel plans, advice about Timothy, Apollos and Stephanas, and ends with greetings and a blessing.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul asks the Corinthians to do about the collection and how the letter closes (1 Corinthians 16)?
ev: Describe how the collection was to be given (16:1-2)
Name the co-workers Paul mentions
Quote the closing words of 16:13-14

nodes.t: The garden of Eden
nodes.d: God plants a garden, places the man in it with a command, and forms the woman as a helper fit for him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the garden and the one thing God told the man not to do?
ev: Retell the formation of the man and the woman
State God's command about the tree (2:16-17)

nodes.t: Exodus: overview
nodes.d: Exodus tells of Israel enslaved in Egypt (1:1-14) and delivered through the plagues, Passover and the sea (chapters 7-15), then of the covenant at Sinai (19-24) and the tabernacle (25-40), ending with the glory of the LORD filling it (40:34-38).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Exodus in order, from the bondage in Egypt to the glory filling the tabernacle?
ev: Name the main sections: bondage, deliverance, the journey to Sinai, the law and covenant, and the tabernacle
Say where Exodus begins (1:1) and ends (40:38)

nodes.t: Led by the pillar of cloud and fire
nodes.d: God leads Israel by the wilderness way and not the near road through Philistia, lest they see war and return. Moses carries the bones of Joseph, and the LORD goes before them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how God led Israel out of Egypt, day and night?
ev: Say why God did not lead them by the nearest road (13:17)
Describe how the LORD led them by day and by night (13:21-22)

nodes.t: Crossing the Red Sea
nodes.d: Pharaoh pursues Israel with chariots and traps them at the sea. Moses says to stand still and see the LORD's salvation; the LORD divides the sea, Israel walks through on dry ground, and the returning waters cover Pharaoh's army.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the crossing of the sea and what Moses told the people to do?
ev: Say what the people said when they saw the Egyptians (14:10-12)
Say what Moses answered (14:13-14)
Say what happened to the Egyptians and how Israel responded (14:27-31)

nodes.t: Bread from heaven: manna and quails
nodes.d: Israel murmurs for the food of Egypt. The LORD sends quails in the evening and manna in the morning, a day's portion to be gathered daily, with a double portion on the sixth day for the sabbath. An omer of manna is kept before the Testimony.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the manna was gathered each day and what was different on the sixth and seventh days?
ev: Say what the people were to do each day and on the sixth day (16:4-5, 16:22-26)
Say what happened to manna kept overnight against the command (16:19-20)
Say how long Israel ate manna (16:35)

nodes.t: Water from the rock at Massah and Meribah
nodes.d: At Rephidim there is no water, and the people chide Moses and test the LORD. At the LORD's direction Moses strikes the rock at Horeb and water comes out; the place is named Massah and Meribah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the people said at Rephidim and how God provided water?
ev: Say what the people asked (17:7)
Say what Moses did and what came of it (17:5-6)

nodes.t: The golden calf
nodes.d: When Moses delays on the mountain, the people ask Aaron to make gods for them. Aaron collects their gold earrings and fashions a molten calf, builds an altar and proclaims a feast, and the people offer sacrifices and rise up to play.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the people did while Moses was on the mountain?
ev: Say what the people asked and what Aaron made (32:1-4)
Say what Aaron proclaimed (32:5)

nodes.t: Numbers: overview
nodes.d: Numbers follows Israel from Sinai through the wilderness: the census, camp and Levites, departure from Sinai, the rebellion at Kadesh and forty years of wandering, Balaam, a second census, and preparation on the plains of Moab for entering the land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short summary of where Israel starts and ends in Numbers?
ev: Describe the journey in Numbers in three stages: at Sinai, wandering, and on the plains of Moab.

nodes.t: The plague stopped by incense
nodes.d: Numbers 16:36-50 records the censers beaten into a covering for the altar, the congregation murmuring against Moses and Aaron, a plague killing 14,700, and Aaron running with a censer between the dead and the living to make atonement.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Aaron stopped the plague?
ev: Say what was done with the censers and what Aaron did to stop the plague.

nodes.t: The fiery serpents and the bronze serpent
nodes.d: Numbers 21:4-9 tells how the people speak against God and Moses, the LORD sends fiery serpents, the people confess, and Moses makes a bronze serpent on a pole so that anyone bitten who looks at it lives.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the story of the bronze serpent and say what the people had to do to live?
ev: Say what the people said, what the LORD sent, and how those bitten were healed.

nodes.t: Baal of Peor and Phinehas
nodes.d: Numbers 25 tells how Israel at Shittim joins in the worship of Baal of Peor and sins with Moabite women, a plague kills 24,000 until Phinehas acts zealously, and the LORD gives him his covenant of peace and an everlasting priesthood and commands Israel to vex the Midianites.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what sin brought a plague at Peor and what Phinehas did?
ev: Say what Israel did at Shittim and how the plague stopped.
Say what the LORD gave Phinehas (25:11-13).

nodes.t: Punishment limits, the ox and the brother's widow
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 25:1-12 limits a beating to forty stripes, forbids muzzling an ox that treads out the corn, gives the duty of a brother to raise up a name for a dead brother and the shoe-loosing ceremony if he refuses, and a rule about a wife seizing a man in a fight.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the purpose of the law of the brother's widow in 25:5-10?
ev: Say the limit on flogging and the reason (25:3).
Describe the duty of a living brother to a dead brother's childless widow.

nodes.t: Job: overview
nodes.d: Job opens with a righteous man losing everything (1-2), moves through his lament and long exchanges with three friends (3-31), Elihu (32-37) and the LORD answering from the whirlwind (38-41), and ends with Job’s repentance and restoration (42).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline the book of Job in four or five parts and name who speaks in each?
ev: Outline the book of Job in its main parts: prologue, speeches, the LORD’s answer, epilogue.

nodes.t: Eliphaz’s first speech
nodes.d: Eliphaz says the innocent do not perish and those who sow wickedness reap it, tells of a night vision asking whether mortal man can be more just than God, and urges Job to seek God and not despise his correction.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} state Eliphaz’s main argument to Job in chapters 4-5?
ev: Identify Eliphaz’s argument in 4:7-8 and his advice in 5:8 and 5:17.

nodes.t: Psalms: overview
nodes.d: The Psalms are 150 songs and prayers addressed to or about the LORD: cries for help, confession, thanksgiving, praise of his creation and rule, songs about the king, and meditation on his law; the book closes with calls to praise (146-150).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name three kinds of psalm and read one verse from a psalm of each kind?
ev: Name several kinds of psalm (lament, thanksgiving, praise, royal, wisdom) and give one psalm number for each.

nodes.t: Psalm 8: what is man? the LORD’s majesty and man’s place
nodes.d: The speaker praises the LORD’s excellent name, considers the heavens, the moon and stars, and asks what man is that God remembers him, saying God made him a little lower than the angels, crowned with glory, with dominion over the works of his hands.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} read Psalm 8:3-6 and say what it teaches about God and man?
ev: Read 8:3-8 and list what is put under man’s dominion.

nodes.t: Psalm 24: the King of glory
nodes.d: The earth is the LORD’s and all in it; those with clean hands and a pure heart may ascend his hill, and the gates are told to lift up their heads for the King of glory, the LORD of hosts.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who may stand in the LORD’s holy place and who the King of glory is in Psalm 24?
ev: Read 24:3-6 and say who may ascend, and 24:7-10 and say who comes in.

nodes.t: Psalm 94: O LORD God, to whom vengeance belongeth
nodes.d: The speaker calls on God as judge of the earth to reward the proud, asks how long the wicked will triumph and kill the widow and fatherless, says the LORD who made the ear hears and he will not cast off his people, and the LORD is his defence.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker says in Psalm 94:9 and 94:14?
ev: Read 94:1-7 and 94:8-15 and 94:16-23 and say what the speaker asks and what he trusts.

nodes.t: Isaiah: overview
nodes.d: Isaiah son of Amoz sees visions concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah; the book moves from indictment and judgment to comfort, a servant, and new heavens and a new earth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who Isaiah was and describe, using Isaiah 1:1 and 40:1-2, how the book moves from rebuke to comfort?
ev: Name the four kings of Judah named in Isaiah 1:1
Describe the shift in tone between chapters 1-39 and chapter 40 using the texts

nodes.t: The valley of vision and Shebna
nodes.d: Jerusalem is distressed by a day of trouble; the people prepare defenses but do not look to the LORD and say let us eat and drink; Shebna is removed and Eliakim receives the key of the house of David.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jerusalem does in Isaiah 22:8-13 and what the LORD says about it?
ev: Say what the people do and fail to do in Isaiah 22:8-13
Explain what happens to Shebna and Eliakim (22:15-25)

nodes.t: A feast on the mountain and death swallowed up
nodes.d: The LORD makes a feast for all peoples on his mountain, removes the veil over all nations, swallows up death, wipes away tears, and the redeemed say they waited for him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD does for all peoples on his mountain in Isaiah 25:6-9?
ev: Describe the feast and the veil (25:6-7)
Quote what the LORD does to death and tears (25:8)
Say what the people say in 25:9

nodes.t: Woe to Ephraim's drunkards and the scoffers in Jerusalem
nodes.d: Isaiah rebukes the drunken leaders, who mock his teaching, boast of a covenant with death, and are promised a tested cornerstone laid in Zion; the farmer's patient work illustrates God's wise ways.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the scoffers in Isaiah 28:15 relied on and what the LORD lays in Zion in 28:16?
ev: Describe the scoffers' covenant with death (28:15)
Quote what the LORD lays in Zion (28:16)
Explain the farmer illustration in 28:23-29

nodes.t: Woe to Ariel: a sealed vision and a marvellous work
nodes.d: The LORD besieges Ariel, the city where David dwelt, then saves it from the nations; the people honour him with lips but not hearts, the vision is like a sealed book, and the deaf will hear and the blind see.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what 29:13 says about the people's worship?
ev: Describe the siege and sudden deliverance of Ariel (29:1-8)
Explain the charge in 29:13
Describe the change promised in 29:17-24

nodes.t: Comfort my people: the incomparable God
nodes.d: God tells his prophets to comfort Jerusalem because her iniquity is pardoned, a voice prepares the way of the LORD, the LORD comes as shepherd, and no one compares to him who gives strength to the weary.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD comforts Jerusalem in Isaiah 40:1-2 and who the LORD is compared to in 40:12-26?
ev: Quote the command and reason in Isaiah 40:1-2
Describe the voice crying in the wilderness (40:3-5)
Explain what 40:28-31 says about those who wait on the LORD

nodes.t: A prayer of remembrance and lament
nodes.d: The prophet recalls the LORD's kindnesses and how Israel rebelled and he became their enemy, then prays for him to look down and come down, confessing sin, and says "we are the clay and thou our potter."
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the prayer of Isaiah 63:15-64:12 and what the people confess?
ev: Recall what the LORD did for his people (63:7-14)
Quote the confession in 64:6
Quote 64:8

nodes.t: Weeping prophet; let him glory that he knows me
nodes.d: Jeremiah longs to weep for the slain of his people, who speak deceit; the LORD announces desolation and says the wise, mighty and rich should not glory in those things but in knowing him as one who exercises lovingkindness, judgment and righteousness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD says a person should glory in according to Jeremiah 9:23-24?
ev: Quote Jeremiah 9:1
Say what the LORD says to glory in (9:23-24)
Explain 9:25-26

nodes.t: Hosea: overview
nodes.d: Hosea's word to Israel in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash and Judah's kings: a prophet's marriage to an unfaithful wife pictures the LORD's love for faithless Israel, followed by charges, judgment and a call to return.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences how Hosea's marriage pictures the LORD's relationship with Israel?
ev: Say that Hosea's marriage (chs 1-3) is an acted picture of the LORD and Israel
Outline the book as marriage (1-3), charges and judgment (4-13) and a closing call to return (14)

nodes.t: No saviour beside the LORD
nodes.d: Ephraim's idol worship brings him to vanish like morning cloud; the LORD alone is God and Saviour from Egypt, yet he will come as a lion and bear, though he also promises to ransom them from the grave and death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Hosea 13:4 says there is no saviour but the LORD?
ev: Summarise 13:4 and 13:9 in your own words
Describe the judgment pictures of 13:7-8
Point to the ransom promise of 13:14
